name: Gonadorelin

lead: Gonadorelin is lab-made GnRH, the brain signal that makes the pituitary release LH and FSH. On TRT forums it is used in place of hCG to keep the testes active, aiming for less testicular shrinkage and steadier hormones.

It binds GnRH receptors on the pituitary, triggering LH and FSH release. Doctors have used it for diagnostic testing and, as pulsed infusions, to restore ovulation or fertility in people with GnRH deficiency. No trial has compared it with hCG in men on testosterone, and users report mixed results.

paras: TRT users take it on a regular schedule alongside testosterone, as a substitute for hCG, often prescribed by clinics that offer TRT. Because it is cleared within minutes, how it is pulsed matters.

Documented trials are in specialist reproductive settings. In TRT use, reports are anecdotal, some users describe persistent atrophy, and continuous exposure desensitises receptors. Supply may come from clinics or compounding sources of varying regulation.

angle.text: Gonadorelin is synthetic GnRH that TRT users take in place of hCG to prompt LH and FSH release, keeping the testes active and limiting testicular shrinkage. It is established in fertility medicine and diagnostics; forum posters report mixed results in TRT.

lead: Gonadorelin is the synthetic form of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), the hypothalamic decapeptide that prompts the pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) [1]. In medicine it has been used to test pituitary responsiveness and, delivered in pulses, to induce ovulation in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea [2][1].

In testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) and bodybuilding communities, gonadorelin is discussed as a substitute for hCG to keep the testes stimulated and avoid atrophy while on exogenous testosterone. Some clinics prescribe it for this purpose, and forum users report mixed experiences [3][4][5].

Published trials cover diagnostic and fertility uses in patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism or amenorrhea [2][6][7]. No trial found here has compared gonadorelin with hCG in men on testosterone therapy, and none has examined appearance outcomes.
infobox: GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) analogue, identical to native GnRH
Injection or infusion; peptide is unstable when taken by mouth [13]
GnRH structure elucidated 1971 (Schally, Guillemin); Nobel Prize 1977 [1]

paras: Gonadorelin has been used as a diagnostic stimulation test of the pituitary and to treat anovulation from GnRH deficiency [1]. A multicenter trial of pulsatile intravenous gonadorelin (Lutrepulse) in 109 women with hypothalamic amenorrhea reported ovulation in 91% and 96% of the primary and secondary amenorrhea groups [2]. Other registered studies have used pulsatile GnRH in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and in women with polycystic ovary syndrome [8][9]. It is also used in veterinary reproduction, particularly in dairy cattle protocols [10][11].

Gonadorelin binds GnRH receptors on pituitary gonadotroph cells and triggers LH and FSH release. It is cleared rapidly, so its physiological effect depends on pulsatile delivery; continuous exposure instead desensitises the receptor, which is the principle behind long-acting GnRH analogues such as leuprolide, goserelin and triptorelin [1][12]. Peptides of this class are degraded in the gut, which is why oral delivery research is ongoing [13][14].

Users on TRT describe being prescribed gonadorelin in place of hCG to maintain testicular size and fertility [3][4][15]. Reported experiences vary. Some users who switched from hCG describe continued atrophy or aching [4][5], citing the peptide's short half-life, while others use it with testosterone for fertility goals [16]. Some rotate it with kisspeptin-10 when hCG is not tolerated [17]. A user seeking information on gonadorelin acetate notes difficulty finding clear efficacy data [18]. These are anecdotes, not controlled data.

Clinical research on gonadorelin concerns reproductive medicine: pulsatile therapy in hypothalamic amenorrhea [2], hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [6][7][8], PCOS infertility [9], and neoadjuvant hormone treatment in infants with undescended testes, in which a randomized trial examined safety [19]. A pump-delivery pharmacokinetic study was withdrawn before enrolment [20]. No human trial identified here has tested gonadorelin as an hCG substitute in men receiving testosterone, or for physique or appearance outcomes.

Pulsatile gonadorelin in the amenorrhea trial was reported to have a low rate of complications [2]. Safety in the self-directed TRT context has not been studied in published trials; forum users report injection-site and hormone-related side effects inconsistently [5][4].

lore.intro: Gonadorelin is discussed in TRT threads as an hCG alternative for preserving testicular function [3][4][21].
